---
title: "Online principal-subspace estimation with adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo"
subtitle: "A controlled stochastic approximation analysis"
author:
  - name: "Jordan Simbananiye"
    affiliations:
      - name: "University College London — CCMI CDT"
date: last-modified
abstract: |
  We analyse global online principal-subspace adaptation in Metropolis sampling
  where the proposal covariance depends jointly on the learned covariance and
  Oja subspace. The mean and covariance updates follow Andrieu and Moulines,
  and an additional Stiefel-valued iterate uses the same accepted states and
  a polar retraction.  We identify the common
  averaged vector field, establish a uniform second-order bound for the
  retraction error, and give an explicit weighted Poisson decomposition of
  the controlled Markov fluctuations.  A localized convergence theorem
  shows that, on eventually compact parameter trajectories, the estimates
  approach the target moments and the Oja iterate approaches the collection
  of invariant subspaces of the target covariance, despite feedback from the
  learned subspace to the kernel.  A composite Lyapunov
  function based on the expected PCA reconstruction error gives an exact global
  dissipation identity for the averaged coupled system.
  The remaining global stochastic stability question for the fully
  feedback-coupled algorithm is isolated explicitly.
keywords:
  - adaptive MCMC
  - online PCA
  - Oja iteration
  - stochastic approximation
  - Poisson equation
  - retraction
---
